mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity prices, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprises in late-cycle expansion
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same post-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05), or the 5-day return is positive despite the rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations, prompting risk-averse investors to sell equities, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during the same month, or ΔCPIAUCSL is not followed by a negative return window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration in PAYEMS (ΔPAYEMS > +10% from prior month) indicates stronger wage growth than expected, which raises marginal utility of consumption and compresses equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: Wage growth acceleration in late-cycle labor markets
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the same pay growth acceleration episode, or wage acceleration is not followed by equity outperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% month-over-month suggests weakening aggregate demand, which lowers equity risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < prev AND RSAFS < prev by ≥2%
regime_hint: Concurrent demand-side softness in manufacturing and retail
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the same dual contraction episode (t-test p < 0.05), or either HOUST or RSAFS recovers before the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 1% signals tighter supply conditions in the manufacturing sector, which raises real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or are not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05) during the same INDPRO decline episode.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it indicates a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and spending, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the two-month UNRATE decline period.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) by at least 2% over a quarter suggests economic softening that reduces growth expectations and equity risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or are not statistically significant during the same GDP contraction quarter (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds INDPRO by more than 15% in a month, it reflects a strong labor-demand environment that supports corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the same month when the labor-demand ratio exceeds the threshold.
